key_insight: OmniAct proposes one manipulation policy that adapts to different robots by directly considering each robot’s kinematics within a scene. The idea is to share task knowledge while tailoring behavior to how each robot can move.
problem_solved: Shared action representations can help transfer skills between robots, but they do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should change manipulation strategies.
method: Use a shared policy for manipulation across different robot embodiments.
Condition the policy directly on each robot’s kinematics in the specific scene.
Adapt manipulation behavior to the robot’s capabilities rather than relying only on a shared action representation.
impact: This approach could make robot policies more reusable across hardware while preserving embodiment-specific behavior. The supplied abstract does not report experimental results or establish the scale of deployment.
visual_elements: Several differently shaped robot arms connected to one central policy, illustrating shared control.
A robot’s joint-and-link diagram alongside a scene image, both feeding into the policy.
Different robots approaching the same object with distinct motion paths, illustrating capability-aware strategies.
A conceptual comparison: shared action representation alone versus scene-specific kinematic conditioning.
paper_title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
paper_authors: Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Jiayuan Yan, Bohan Fang, Wisdom Oluchi Ikezogwo
